defect.title: Design-lineage conflict: a byte-frozen artifact inherited from v1.6 is validated against the v1.7 design SHA
defect.raising_site: scripts/build_p4_2a_gold_sample.py line 2511, inside validate_dev_final_prediction_freeze, reached from scripts/evaluate_p4_2a_gold.py line 2367
defect.mechanism: validate_dev_final_prediction_freeze builds expected_manifest with design_sha256 set to design.sha256, the SHA of the currently loaded design. The dev-final predictions manifest records design_sha256 57e04f99a8ee91b64fe0aa4dc479e95c3de65fd31f04ac6c5879d4f81e5539c9, because those predictions were produced on 2026-08-04 under the v1.6 design. Loaded under v1.7 (SHA 4c7964ad547820f5672631939af93978f11cb9f91e5921087770ac7d0d79bec1) the comparison can never succeed.
defect.the_design_already_declares_the_answer: config/p4_event_evaluation_v1_7.yaml declares extends_design with path config/p4_event_evaluation_v1_6.yaml, sha256 57e04f99...39c9 and schema_version p4.2a-evaluation-design-v1.6, plus an inheritance block marking active_prediction_contract, prompt, model, evaluation_thresholds and related items byte_frozen. The declared ancestor SHA is byte-identical to the value the manifest carries. The design states the lineage correctly; the validator ignores it.
defect.why_the_value_is_not_available_at_valida: load_evaluation_design resolves and merges the ancestor design and does not retain extends_design in the loaded document; the merged document's top-level keys contain no extends_design entry. The ancestor SHA is therefore known at load time but discarded before validation.
defect.same_family_as_previous_blocker: This is the second instance of the same class recorded today. The first was the combine-owner artifact-role conflict; both arise from validators that ignore an artifact's declared role or lineage. Both are latent rather than regressions: under v1.6 the manifest's design SHA equalled the loaded design SHA, so the check passed and the defect only surfaces once the design version advances while the artifact stays byte-frozen.
defect.not_previously_exercised: No report exists under docs/phase4/eval/reports for any version, so the heldout evaluation has never run end to end under any design.

explicitly_refused_actions: Editing config/p4_event_evaluation_v1_7.yaml to restate the dev-final design SHA: its SHA 4c7964ad...bec1 is bound to the executed one-shot inference state, the candidate predictions and the heldout selection manifest.

Editing the dev-final predictions manifest to carry the v1.7 SHA: it is create-only frozen evidence of a completed v1.6 round, and rewriting it would falsify the record of when those predictions were produced.

Re-running the dev60 final predictions under v1.7 to regenerate a matching manifest: that would spend model calls to manufacture agreement with a validator bug and would break the byte-frozen inheritance the design depends on.
Passing a different design or scope to make the evaluator proceed.
Retrying the one-shot evaluation in any form before the defect is fixed and reviewed.

recommended_remediation.principle: A byte-frozen artifact inherited from an ancestor design must be validated against the design SHA under which it was frozen, which the design already declares in extends_design, not against the SHA of the design currently loaded.
recommended_remediation.proposed_change: Retain the resolved lineage on FrozenEvaluationDesign (for example an ancestor_design_sha256 chain populated from extends_design during load) and, in validate_dev_final_prediction_freeze, accept manifest design_sha256 when it equals the current design SHA or an ancestor SHA in that declared chain. The acceptance must be conditional on the artifact being declared byte_frozen inherited; an arbitrary mismatch must still fail closed. Codex should check whether any sibling validator computes an expected design_sha256 the same way and fix the class rather than this one call site.
recommended_remediation.why_this_is_code_not_design: The fix lives in scripts/build_p4_2a_gold_sample.py, so the frozen design bytes and SHA are untouched and every binding to the executed one-shot inference is preserved.
mandatory_conditions: Pre-register the fix before use: commit the code change and offline fixture tests first, then run the evaluation once.
Add a regression test that a manifest carrying an unrelated design SHA still fails closed, so the fix does not degrade into accepting any SHA.
Do not change any threshold, metric definition, selection rule, prompt, model, prediction contract or evaluation design.
The combine-owner outputs already produced must not be regenerated or overwritten; they are create-only and their digests are recorded above.
The heldout evaluation remains one-shot with zero retries and has not yet been consumed.

state_ready_for_evaluation_once_unblocke.note: The same invocation should succeed once the lineage validation is fixed; no input needs to change.
